summary:
# NOTES ON THE TWO BOOKS

## BOOK 1: "The Datchet Diamonds" by Richard Marsh (Gutenberg 40353; illustrated by Stanley L. Wood; frontispiece "Shall I shoot all three of you?" p.265)

**Chapters:** I Two Men and a Maid; II Overheard in the Train; III The Diamonds; IV Miss Wentworth's Rudeness; V In the Bodega; VI The Adventures of a Night; VII The Datchet Diamonds Are Placed in Safe Custody; VIII In the Moment of His Success; IX A Proposal of Marriage; X Cyril's Friend; XI John Ireland's Warrant; XII A Woman Roused; XIII The Detective and the Lady; XIV Among Thieves; XV Put to the Question; XVI A Modern Instance of an Ancient Practice; XVII The Most Dangerous Foe of All; XVIII The Last of the Datchet Diamonds; XIX A Woman's Logic.

**Characters:**
- Daisy (Miss Strong): lover of Cyril; friend of Charlie. Mother left her £120/yr. Works? (no; Charlie earns ~£500/yr writing for *Fashion*).
- Cyril Paxton: stockbroker-speculator ("punter"), gambles in Eries (lost), Trumpit Gold Mine shares (bought 10,000 shares, had been at discount). Memory for faces. Has rented safe at Chancery Lane Deposit Company. Staying at Makell's Hotel, Brighton.
- Miss Charlotte Wentworth ("Charlie"): 30, journalist, wears pince-nez, Medina Villas house shared with Daisy; sardonic.
- Mr. Franklyn: ~40, grey-streaked black hair, solicitor/lawyer, Cyril's friend; holds 10,000 Trumpit shares in strongbox.
- Mr. Lawrence (real name Reginald Hargraves, alias "The Toff"): fair, blue eyes, soft voice; thief; met Daisy on Devil's Dyke via umbrella; proposes to Daisy in Ch. IX.
- The Baron (Isaac Bergstein): German-American, tall, thin, stoop, huge hat, long black overcoat, claw-like finger, clawlike nails, huge mouth, no chin.
- Stephen Eversleigh: duke's servant, short-sighted, carried diamonds.
- John Ireland: Scotland Yard detective; bets Franklyn £100 at evens Paxton has guilty knowledge.
- Hollier (George Hollier): police officer tailing Franklyn.
- Bill Cooper: informer, "Tom the Toff" and "the Baron" nicked diamonds.
- Skittles: henchman with pail; Dick? No.
- Treadwater: hotel manager at Makell's.
- Duchess of Datchet; Duke of Datchet; diamonds valued £250,000 (Amsterdam Necklace ~£100,000; Datchet Tiara; Begum's Brooch; Banee's Bracelet).

**Plot events (order):**
1. Pier, Brighton: Daisy meets Lawrence (met on Devil's Dyke, umbrella in rain, Masonic Ball at Dome). Cyril arrives, quarrels; Cyril says he has "a big bull" on Eries and will know best or worst by tomorrow; "Next week I emigrate." Daisy kisses him.
2. Train to London: Cyril reads of Duchess of Datchet's diamonds robbed (despatch box vanished; Windsor→Paddington→Grosvenor Sq; Bartlett's Bank). Overhears via swung glass pane Lawrence and Baron: Eversleigh's spectacles, detective camera copy spectacle case, swapped despatch-boxes at Windsor station. Cyril also swaps Gladstone bags at Brighton refreshment room with Lawrence's bag (brown, new); finds diamonds in his bag.
3. Cyril hides diamonds in evening paper inside Lawrence's bag; puts that bag at Makell's. Tells Daisy at pier he may have quarter-million. Daisy proposes marriage within a month; Charlie quarrels with Cyril ("kitchen-maid" remark; "Mr Paxton... dishonest" accusation). Cyril leaves angrily.
4. Bodega: Baron and Lawrence confront Cyril about "Gladstone bag" colour; Ireland appears; warns about the diamonds' unsaleability; Ireland says he knows where diamonds are.
5. Night: Cyril followed; burglars try lock, then ladder at window; Cyril fires revolver; ladder left behind.
6. Cyril takes diamonds to Chancery Lane safe. Trumpit shares rise to £10. Morning: man at Central Station tries to take bag; Cyril rids himself.
7. Evening: Gladstone bag claimed by shabby man ("sent by Mr Paxton"); Cyril abducted by chloroform outside hotel en route to Daisy.
8. Daisy waits on pier; Lawrence proposes; says Cyril stopping in town. Daisy & Charlie fight. Franklyn arrives: Cyril's Trumpit shares at £12 10s; Franklyn goes to Makell's.
9. Ireland has warrant for Paxton's arrest; bets Franklyn £100; Hollier shadows Franklyn. Ireland shows ring Paxton dropped (from Cyril's handkerchief). Searches Makell's Gladstone bag, finds nothing.
10. Daisy and Charlie go to Medina Villas... Bill Cooper: "Tom the Toff" and "the Baron" have Paxton at "a crib." Ireland takes cab with Daisy and Cooper toward Downs; police waggonette.
11. Cyril (in Ch XIV) tied, burnt with branding iron "thief," Baron tortures with revolver; Lawrence interrogates; Cyril fights, knocks out Baron & Lawrence; lamp smashed; fire; Cyril writes will leaving all to Daisy Strong.
12. Rescue: Daisy finds Cyril's hand through window with will; police arrive. Cyril recovers; reveals diamonds; Ireland recovers diamonds from Chancery Lane safe.
13. Trial: Hargraves (Lawrence) and Bergstein (Baron) each 20 years penal servitude. Cyril married Daisy quietly at Brighton church; Cyril invested Trumpit proceeds in consols.

## BOOK 2: "'Gainst the Might of Spain" by Percy F. Westerman (Gutenberg 78984; illus. Savile Lumley; Pilgrim Press; frontispiece "The Escape", p.154)

**Chapters I–XXV:** I The Pilot Who Did Not Return; II The *Damsel of Lyme*; III Captain Hannibal Cleat; IV Jack Staynton; V Captain Cleat in His True Colours; VI A Pirate in Spite of Myself; VII Catching a Tartar; VIII Captured!; IX Don Iago d'Alvarez; X Aboard the *San Josef*; XI The Inquisition; XII In the Torture-Chamber; XIII The Escape; XIV A Timely Rescue; XV Off to the Spanish Main; XVI The Mountain Pass; XVII Bringing Back the Silver; XVIII At Bay; XIX The Taking of the Galleon; XX Bringing in the Prize; XXI The Great Armada; XXII English Dogs and Spanish Bulls; XXIII The Fireships; XXIV The Last of the *Damsel of Lyme*; XXV In the Queen's Presence.

**Narrator:** Ralph Roy, b. 6 July 1568, Crofton, Hampshire. Father Richard Roy, Queen's pilot (once brought Philip of Spain's ship to Southampton). Mother unnamed (called "Mistress Roy"). Father vanished night of a "Brixham pinnace *Speedie*" call (Ralph aged 12); a cloak-and-dagger deception by Don Iago d'Alvarez & José da Silva, who sold him to Philip.

**Key people:** Roger Staynton (master-gunner of Portsmouth, Sir Henry Radclyffe governor, Mayor John Highfield); son Jack Staynton (two years older than Ralph; shorter, broad). Captain Hannibal Cleat (pirate; apprentice contract £5; bought the *Damsel of Lyme* for £34 at auction). Mate James (red-faced, curly-headed, bad temper); "Old Garge" (kind seaman); Dick Buzza (Cornish boy, 10, sole survivor of sloop *Jane* of Padstow); Coombes (mate, Bosham native); Skelton (seaman); Jenkins (seaman rescued from cliff); Master Matthews; Sir Thomas Slingsby (later plain Tom); Don Iago d'Alvarez (Spanish grandee); Don José da Silva (Spanish captain, killed at Fowey action); Don Pedro Valdez; Captain Prowse; Captain Young; Lord Howard of Effingham; Queen Elizabeth.

**Events (order):**
1. Ralph's father sails on night storm; Ralph 14 bound 'prentice; moved to Portsmouth.
2. *Damsel of Lyme* arrested pinnace; Captain Cleat hires Ralph; Jack hides in cabin hatch; Cleat whips Ralph at mast; revealed Cleat is pirate; re-crews with condemned men.
3. Pirate career: sloop *Jane* sunk (Dick Buzza saved); Cornwall; Brittany; galleon attack (Cleat fatally wounded); Ralph sails alone; captured by Spaniards of the *San José*/*San Josef* (Don Iago). Captain Cleat's corpse dumped; gold hidden in limbers.
4. Ralph imprisoned in bilboes on *San Josef*; ship storm; Vigo harbour; villa of Don Iago; tower study with Ric Roy's chart of Southampton Water (dated A.D. 1552).
5. Inquisition: Ralph's cell No. 19; father found in next cell; father reveals his capture; Ralph condemned as heretic/sacrilegist; father kills pikemen and Inquisitors; escape disguised as familiars through chapel of St. Thomé; steal *Damsel of Lyme*; galley chase; rescued by *Nonsuch* of Dartmouth (Roger Staynton, Jack).
6. Fowey storm; sail to Mexico (Rio del Foy, San Luis mine). Father wounded? No—father fights mules on pass; rescue Jenkins.
7. Silver extracted; Spaniard ambush; trench at neck of land; Coombes swims pinnace across; Ralph wounded (left leg, head) during sally led by Jack; Skelton carries him.
8. Virginia visit; *Sol del Esto* galleon captured (Ralph captures with 10 men; 300 prisoners; father loses left foot; Don José da Silva killed). Return via Lizard to Portsmouth.
9. 1588 Armada alarm: Ralph, Jack, Sir Thomas Slingsby (Tom) join; Plymouth; *Damsel* engages Fleming's pirate; Admiral Howard; Drake's squadron; Don Pedro Valdez surrenders galleon; Venetian ship at Goodwins; Damsel boarded, Ralph wounded; fireship attack off Calais, *Damsel* burned sinking two galleons.
10. Ralph reports to Queen Elizabeth (Whitehall); knighted "Sir Ralph Roy"; Sussex (Radclyffe) vouches. Later: Don Iago captured as galley slave at Bordeaux, appeals to Ralph.

# Notes for use
- Book 1 is a detective/sensation story; Book 2 is a historical sea adventure. Keep separate.
